entries.t: Establishment of Pineapple Processing Industry in Assam
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 6433 
ANSWERED ON 02ND APRIL, 2026 
  
ESTABLISHMENT OF PINEAPPLE PROCESSING INDUSTRY IN ASSAM 
6433.  SHRI PARIMAL SUKLABAIDYA: 
Will the Minister of FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the Government is aware that the Lakhipur area in Cachar district of Assam 
produces a significant quantity of pineapples and has strong potential for agro -based 
industries and if so, the details thereof; 
(b)  whether the Ministry has any proposal, plan or scheme to establish pineapple processing 
or food processing industries in the Lakhipur region so that the benefits of this produce 
can reach markets across the country; and 
(c)  if so, the details thereof and if  not, the reasons therefor along with the steps proposed 
to promote food processing industries in the region? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR FOOD PROCESSING INDUSTRIES 
(SHRI RAVNEET SINGH) 
    
(a) to (c): In order to promote and facilitate overall development of the food processing sector, 
Ministry of Food Processing Industries (MoFPI)  has been incentivizing setting up of related 
industries through its two Central Sector Scheme s viz. Pradhan Mantri Kisan SAMPADA 
Yojana (PMKSY) & Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry 
(PLISFPI) and a Centrally sponsored Pradhan Mantri Formalization of Micro Food Processing 
Enterprises (PMFME) scheme across the country including Lakhipur area in Cachar district of 
Assam. These schemes are not region specific but demand driven.  MoFPI does not setup any 
food processing Industries on its own. However, MoFPI extends financial support to 
prospective entrepreneurs for setting up of different kinds of food processing industries 
including processing of pineapple, as per respective scheme guidelines.  
 
To promote processing of local produce including pineapple processing, One District 
One Product (ODOP) approach has been adopted under Pr adhan Mantri  Formalization of 
Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) scheme, to reap the benefit of scale in terms of 
procurement of inputs, availing common services and marketing of products. It provides the 
framework for value chain development and alignment of support infrastructure. “Pineapple” 
has been identified as ODOP in Cachar district of Assam.  
 
In the State of Assam, a s on 31.12.2025, MoFPI has sanctioned 72 food processing 
projects under corresponding component schemes of PMKSY, out of which 1 project is located 
in Cachar district. Four food processing companies have been approved for assistance under 
various categories of the PLISFPI scheme in Assam State. Further, 5194 micro food processing 
enterprises have been approved for assistance under PMFME, out of which 358 are located in 
Cachar district. 
 
*****

entries.t: Road Construction and Upgradation Works in Lakshadweep
entries.head:
GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 6434 
ANSWERED ON 2ND APRIL, 2026 
  
ROAD CONSTRUCTION AND UPGRADATION WORKS IN LAKSHADWEEP 
  
6434.   SHRI MUHAMMED HAMDULLAH SAYEED  
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
  
(a) the details of road construction and upgradation works carried out 
in various islands in Lakshadweep during the last ten years, island -
wise. 
(b) the  total length of New roads constructed, roads widened and 
roads repaired or resurfaced in this period; 
(c) the funds allocated, released and utilized for road infrastructure 
development in Lakshadweep during the last ten years; 
(d) the challenges faced in road construction and maintenance in 
island territories like Lakshadweep including land availability, terrain 
and climatic conditions; and 
(e) the steps being taken by the Government to improve road 
connectivity. transportation efficiency and safety across the islands of 
Lakshadweep? 
  
 
 
 
 
  

ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) & (b)   The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways   is primarily 
responsible for development and maintenance of National Highways 
(NHs) and also provides financial assistance to States/Union 
Territories for development of State roads (other than rural roads) 
under the Central Road and Infrastructure Fund (CRIF) based on their 
priorities. 
There are no National Highways in the Union Territor y of 
Lakshadweep; accordingly, no works relating to construction, 
upgradation, widening or resurfacing of NHs have been 
undertaken  during the last ten years. 
The road network in Lakshadweep comprises internal roads, which are 
developed and maintained by t he UT Administration. As per 
information provided by Lakshadweep Public Works Department, 
11.889 km of roads have been constructed and 13.605 km have been 
resurfaced during the last ten years. 
(c)  No funds have been allocated, released or utilised   for National 
Highway infrastructure development in Lakshadweep during the last 
ten years. No proposal has been received from the UT Administration 
for funding under CRIF. 
(d)  Road development in island territories such as Lakshadweep 
faces challenges including limited land availability, ecological 
restrictions, coastal and low -lying terrain, logistical constraints in 
transportation of materials, and adverse climatic conditions such as 
high humidity and saline environment. 
(e)  Development and maintenance of internal roads in Lakshadweep 
are the responsibility of the UT Administration. The Central 
Government supports infrastructure development in coordination with

DR. NISHIKANT DUBEY: 
 
Will the Minister of JAL SHAKTI be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the Government has recently reviewed the implementation of the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), 
particularly with regard to providing Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTCs) to rural 
households across the country and if so, the details thereof, State-wise and district-wise, particularly 
in Shahdol, Nabarangpur, Bastar, Bharatpur and Chikkaballapur Lok Sabha Constituencies; 
(b) the number of rural families provided with FHTCs so far across the country, State and district-wise, 
including in the above-mentioned Lok Sabha Constituencies and Districts; 
(c) whether the Government has identified States or districts where the coverage of tap water connections 
is lower than the national average, particularly in Chhattisgarh including tribal and remote areas of 
Bastar division and in Rajasthan including Bharatpur Lok Sabha Constituency and if so, the details 

Page 2 of 3 
 
thereof along with the steps being taken to accelerate the implementation of the said Mission in the 
said areas; 
(d) whether the Government is aware that Ramnagar and Chakramnagar villages, located five kilometers 
away from Bharatpur, have tap water connections but do not have water supply and if so, the details 
thereof along with the steps taken by the Government in this regard; 
(e) the number of projects audited under the said Mission in Rajasthan so far along with the number of 
cases in which irregularities have been found; 
(f) the details of persons or agencies found guilty in such cases of irregularities along with the 
administrative or legal action taken against them so far; and 
(g) the latest update on the progress made under the ‘Nal Se Jal’ Yojana in Bhopal district of Madhya 
Pradesh? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR JAL SHAKTI 
    (SHRI V. SOMANNA)  
(a) to (d) Since August, 2019, Government of India, in partnership with States/ UTs including Madhya 
Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh & Karnataka , is implementing  Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) to 
make provision of potable tap water supply in adequate quantity,  of prescribed quality on regular & 
long-term basis to every rural household in the country. 
At the start the Mission, only 3.23 c rore (16.7%) rural households were reported to have tap water 
connections. So far, as reported by States/ UTs  as on 03.03.2026, under JJM, more than 12.58 c rore 
additional rural households have been provided with tap water connections. Thus, as on 03.03.2026, out 
of around 19.36 c rore rural household s in the country, approx.  15.82 crore (81.71%) households are 
reported to have tap water connections  in their homes. The parliamentary constituency-wise details of 
tap connections provided under JJM are not maintained at the Government of India level.  The State/ 
UT-wise, district-wise and v illage-wise status of tap water  connection provided under the m ission in 
rural areas is in public domain and available on JJM dashboard at:  
https://ejalshakti.gov.in/jjmreport/JJMIndia.aspx   
A number of steps have been taken to implement JJM in the whole country , including those in tribal 
areas, with speed, which inter alia, includes joint discussions and finalization of saturation plans and 
annual action plans (AAP) of States/UTs, regular review of implementation, workshops / conferences / 
webinars capacity building, training, knowledge sharing, field visits by multi -disciplinary team to 
provide technical support, etc. For online monitoring, JJM–Integrated Management Information System 
(IMIS) and JJM–Dashboard has been put in place. Provision has also been made for transparent online 
financial management through Public Financial Management System (PFMS). 
The Government of India regularly reviews the implementation JJM with States/UTs through 
conferences, workshops, review meetings, field visits, and other forums. During these reviews, 
States/UTs are advised to expedite the implementation of JJM to ensure objectives of the missions are 
achieved. Further, as stipulated in the operational guidelines, the Government of India also conducts 

Page 3 of 3 
 
third-party functionality assessments across States/UTs. The assessment  reports are shared with the 
respective States/UTs

STATUS OF PMAY-U AND PMAY-U 2.0 IN KARNATAKA AND ASSAM 
 
NO.6438. SMT. BIJULI KALITA MEDHI: 
SHRI P C MOHAN: 
 
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS be pleased to 
state: 
 
(a)  the present status of implementation of Housing for All under 
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana–Urban (PMAY -U) and PMAY -U 2.0, 
district-wise in Assam and Karnataka including Bengaluru; 
(b)  the number of houses sanctioned, completed and handed over 
under PMAY-U during each of the last three years, district -wise in 
Assam and Karnataka including Bengaluru; 
(c)  the targets fixed for sanction and completion of dwelling units 
under PMAY -U 2.0 during the next three years, district -wise in 
Assam and Karnataka including Bengaluru; and 
(d)  whether any shortcomings were identified in implementation of 
PMAY-U in urban centres and if so, the details thereof along with 
the remedial measures incorporated in PMAY -U 2.0 to improve 
delivery, beneficiary identification and timely completion of 
houses, district-wise in Assam and Karnataka including Bengaluru? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF HOUSING AND URBAN AFFAIRS 
(SHRI TOKHAN SAHU) 
 
  (a) to (d):  Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) has been 
implementing  Pradhan  Mantri  Awas Yojana – Urban (PMAY -U)  since  
25.06.2015 with an aim to provide all weather pucca houses with basic civic 
amenities to all eligible urban beneficiaries across the country , including 
the State of Assam and Karnataka.  The scheme period of PMAY -U has been 
extended up to 30
th September 2026 for  completion of under -construction 
houses and release of funds through SNA-SPARSH module. Based on the 
learning from the experiences of implementation of PMAY -U, MoHUA has 
revamped the scheme and launched PMAY -U 2.0 ‘Housing for All’ Mission 
with effect from 01.09.2024 for  implementation in urban areas across the 
country, including the State of Assam and Karnataka, to support 1 crore 
additional eligible beneficiaries in next five years. The scheme is 
implemented through four verticals i.e., Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), 
Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) 
and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS).  
…2/ - 

-2- 
PMAY-U & PMAY -U 2.0 are demand driven schemes and there are no 
fixed targets. States/Union Territories (UTs) assess the requirement 
through their Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/  Implementing Agencies in their 
respective jurisdictions, select the beneficiaries based on the eligibility 
criteria and implement housing project. Based on the demand survey and 
selection of beneficiaries, the project proposals are prepared and 
approved by the State Level Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee 
(SLSMC) headed by the Chief Secretary of States/UTs for further 
consideration of release of Central Assistance by Central Sanctioning 
and Monitoring Committee (CSMC).  
 
The Ministry conducts regular review meetings with States/UTs to ensure 
completion of the remaining under -construction houses within the 
stipulated timeframe. It has been observed that the major challenges faces 
by the implementing agencies include non-availability of encumbrance free  
land, unwillingness of beneficiaries, shortage of skilled manpower, 
financial constraint of implementing agencies, issues related to trunk 
infrastructure, increase in the cost of construction materials, delays in 
obtaining statutory clearance/  No Objection Certificates (NOCs) and 
disruptions caused by unforeseen circumstances.  
 
District-wise details of houses sanctioned, grounded &  
completed/delivered since inception and houses sanctioned &  
completed/delivered during the last three years under PMAY -U and PMAY-U 
2.0 in the States  of Assam and Karnataka including Bengaluru, as on
